subject: problem with space-time interaction where there aren't samples for every time and location

messages.author: 8c6b85a01a12e3e2
messages.subject: problem with space-time interaction where there aren't samples for every time and location
parts:
Hi all, 

I have a problem where the answer might be "you have to model the missing data or you can't do it" but I'm not sure.

I want to infer a model with space-time interaction term like

y ~ 1 + f(week, model="rw2",  replicate = location, control.group=list(model="besag"))

model <- inla( y, data, family = "binomial", Ntrials = n)

but I get an error:

Error in inla(formula_st1, family = "binomial", data = countlist, Ntrials = n, :
There are one or more NA's in 'group' where 'idx' in f(idx,...) is not NA: idx = 'date'

I suspect the cause is that I don't have data for every location at every week.  It's not that the covariates are missing, it's that the number of samples are zero.   

Any advice on how to proceed?

Thanks!

--Mike

messages.author: afb003e064114795
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problem with space-time interaction where there aren't samples for every time and location
parts:
Hi,
I see two issues, both of which I think are fixed by the same fix:
1) you specify replicate but not group
2) besag cannot be a group model (I’m pretty sure)

Solution: make location the main model (besag), set group=week and the control.group model to “rw2”, and don’t use replicate.

Finn

messages.author: 8c6b85a01a12e3e2
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] problem with space-time interaction where there aren't samples for every time and location
parts:
You were on the right track with a basic error, but it wasn't that one.  It turns out the issue was a manifestation of a classic screw-up: never test equality on floats.  When I switch "week" to an integer type from a float, it ran. My guess is "group" was failing because grouping floats isn't guaranteed to work.  Granted, now it throws a warning:

Warning in inla(formula, family = "binomial", data = data, Ntrials = data$nsamples, : f(location, ...): Number of unused groups >= the number of groups used: 42 >= 30, this is *usually* a misspesification

But this is a good thing as I can go back to figuring out if what I'm doing makes sense and not wrestling with not being able to do it at all.

Thanks again for your help. I'm new to INLA and this is an excellent support group.

--Mike
